claim: Secondary report claims Anthropic enforces subscription-auth bans via OAuth/session-token fingerprinting that blocks requests not originating from official web, mobile, or whitelisted-SDK clients.
stance_target: Anthropic uses technical enforcement (not just ToS language) against third-party automation using subscription credentials
scope_conditions: unverified secondary blog summarizing an uncited VentureBeat report
quoted_support: Anthropic's backend now identifies when a credential is being used from an unapproved client or IP fingerprint, blocking requests that don't originate from official interfaces (web app, mobile app, or officially whitelisted SDKs).
time_period: undated (post-ban, specific date not given in this source)

claim: The same report claims suspicious usage patterns, such as high-frequency calls from browser automation tools like Selenium or Puppeteer, are throttled or rejected, and breaching subscriptions may have credentials revoked or accounts suspended.
stance_target: rate-limiting and account suspension are concrete consequences of automating consumer subscription access
scope_conditions: unverified secondary blog, low editorial quality
quoted_support: Automated Rate-Limiting: Suspicious usage patterns—such as high-frequency calls from browser automation or proxies—are throttled or rejected outright... If a subscription is found to be in breach (e.g., used by a third-party SaaS), credentials may be revoked or accounts suspended.

claim: Per this source, unofficial browser plug-ins and third-party SaaS agents that previously worked using Claude subscription credentials now fail authentication with 401/403 errors, while official Claude web/mobile clients remain unaffected.
stance_target: specific technical consequence (401/403 errors) of the ban, distinguishing official client access from automated/third-party access
quoted_support: Popular browser plug-ins that "inject" Claude into Google Docs, VSCode, or custom dashboards fail to authenticate, returning 401 or 403 errors.
